business.title: Identification of plasma lipids as non-invasive signatures for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
business.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the leading cause of chronic liver diseases worldwide, which may progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). To address this growing public health concern, non-invasive diagnostic approaches are needed to identify individuals with MASLD for early detection. We used a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry-based method to quantify plasma lipid species from 99 samples collected from individuals with MASLD (No-MASH, n = 35; MASH, n = 43) and healthy individuals (n = 21) from All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) and National Liver Disease Biobank (NLDB) at Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences (ILBS), New Delhi, India, between 2021 and 2024. We performed statistical analysis to identify lipid signatures, which were confirmed by machine learning (ML) model (Random Forest). Here, we identified 10 lipid signatures for No-MASH and 8 lipid signatures for MASH to distinguish respective groups from healthy individuals, and additionally, 2 lipid signatures that distinguish individuals with No-MASH from MASH on the discovery set (n = 69) with subsequent confirmation on the internal validation set (n = 30) using statistical analysis. Using these signature lipids, ML model achieved combined AUC of 1.0 (95% CI: 1.00-1.00) for healthy versus No-MASH and healthy versus MASH comparisons, whereas an AUC of 0.97 (95% CI: 0.89-1.00) for No-MASH versus MASH comparison. This cross-sectional study highlights remodelling of the MASLD lipidome and demonstrates the potential of plasma-based lipids as non-invasive signatures for disease stratification upon future validation in independent cohorts.

science.title: A robust and reliable method for malware classification using hybrid features and gradient boosting
science.description: The most significant problem facing software security firms in the current cybersecurity system is the fact that new strains of malware keep on appearing. The achievement of successful detection of malicious software based on both static and dynamic data remains unmet despite the further realization of different approaches to deep learning and machine learning. Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power (particularly GPUs) and time. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets. A classification model based on gradient-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in-distribution test samples well. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98.10 and 98.40% using combined datasets. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems.

science.title: Performance-based evaluation of hyperbolic and parabolic vertical curves for highway geometric design
science.description: Vertical curves play a fundamental role in highway geometric design by influencing vehicle dynamics, ride comfort, and safety. Although parabolic curves are widely adopted in current practice, alternative curve formulations may exhibit different dynamic-performance characteristics. To the authors’ knowledge, limited research has examined the vehicle-dynamics implications of hyperbolic vertical curves using multi-body simulation under standard highway-design constraints. Therefore, this study compares the dynamic performance of hyperbolic and parabolic vertical curves using a CarSim-based vehicle model. The analysis covered crest and sag curves designed according to stopping sight distance (SSD) and passing sight distance (PSD) criteria under identical geometric boundary conditions. Vehicle responses were evaluated using four indicators: maximum vertical acceleration, dynamic wheel load, pitch angle, and suspension deflection. The results revealed substantial differences between the two curve formulations. Vertical acceleration was the most sensitive indicator, with hyperbolic curves producing peak responses of up to 0.590 m/s², compared with approximately 0.030 m/s² for the corresponding parabolic curves. Conversely, under sag-curve conditions, hyperbolic curves reduced peak wheel loads by approximately 20–30% and suspension deflections by approximately 15–20% relative to the parabolic alternative. Pitch-angle responses showed only negligible differences between the two formulations. The findings demonstrate a clear performance trade-off between the investigated curve geometries. While the parabolic profile consistently produced lower vertical acceleration, the hyperbolic profile reduced peak wheel load and suspension deflection under the investigated sag-curve conditions. These benefits were accompanied by substantially increased vertical acceleration. The proposed framework provides a performance-based approach for evaluating alternative vertical-curve formulations and supports the integration of vehicle-dynamics considerations into future highway geometric-design studies.

science.title: Directional magnetic field detection with zero-bias surface acoustic wave sensors
science.description: Surface acoustic wave magnetic field sensors are promising candidates in detecting low-amplitude magnetic fields over a broad frequency range. For sensor arrays and portable systems, operating without an external magnetic bias field is essential for reducing system complexity and power consumption. One approach to achieve an internal magnetic bias is to intentionally tilt the magnetic anisotropy of the sensing layer relative to the acoustic wave propagation direction. In this work, we present two types of internally biased surface acoustic wave magnetic field sensors based on exchange-biased multilayer structures. These consist of two multilayer stacks of Ta | (Fe90Co10)78Si12B10 | Ni81Fe19 | Mn80Ir20 | Ta layers that enable a stable magnetic configuration with low magnetic noise in a nearly single magnetic domain state. The best fabricated sensor reaches a detection limit of 69 pT/Hz1/2 at 10 Hz and 22 pT/Hz1/2 at 100 Hz, which is to our knowledge the lowest detection limit reported for SAW magnetic field sensors operated without an external bias field. The sensors exhibit a sinusoidal directional response fitting to an analytical magnetic model that includes magnetic energy contributions from magnetostatic interactions and unidirectional anisotropy.

science.title: Single‑cell and bulk RNA sequencing identifies T cell marker genes to predict the prognosis of ovarian cancer
science.description: Ovarian cancer, with high mortality and often late diagnosis, shows high recurrence despite treatment. The variable effectiveness of immunotherapy highlights the urgent need for personalized, advanced therapeutic strategies. To investigate T-cell marker genes, single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data were sourced from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Additionally, bulk RNA-sequencing data along with clinical information from ovarian cancer patients were retrieved from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database to establish a prognostic signature. This study involved survival analysis to evaluate associations between different risk groups, and explored cellular communication and relevant pathway analyses, including metabolic pathways. We identified 41 genes showing varied expression between two T-cell subclusters, marking subcluster 0 with CCL5 and GZMA, and attributing the rest to subcluster 1. Re-annotation using canonical T-cell lineage and exhaustion markers confirmed subcluster 0 as activated cytotoxic CD8+T cells (CCL5+GZMA+), while subcluster 1 showed an immediate-early/stress-response gene signature rather than a canonical exhausted phenotype. These markers delineate four prognostic groups within the TCGA OV dataset, with T-cluster 2 exhibiting the poorest survival, in contrast to T-cluster 3, which shows the best. We developed a six-gene T-cell scoring model (DUSP2, ATF3, NR4A1, RGS2, RGS1, TNFAIP3), with the low-score group showing significantly better overall survival (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.55–0.99, P = 0.048) and progression-free survival (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.51–0.93, P = 0.012). Moreover, cellular and metabolic pathway analyses underscored the importance of CCL, IL2 and MGMT pathways in these subclusters. The study identifies CCL5 as a biomarker for T-cell subtypes in ovarian cancer using scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data. A T-cell scoring model based on six genes predicts survival and progression rates, and provides incremental prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological factors (multivariable Cox: OS HR = 1.32, P = 0.028; PFS HR = 1.38, P = 0.009). This model could be a candidate prognostic indicator and CCL5 is a candidate biomarker and potential therapeutic target that warrants further functional validation in ovarian cancer.
